missed.fact: Entry has no completedAt, priority, location or all-day column. Completion time is only EntryCompletion.resolvedAt. Priority is the non-null `importance: Int = 0` (0 to 4), so it is 0 rather than null for events. All-day is not a column: it is startTime == null, and ReminderSpec only has an AllDayAnchorPreset.
The merge needs a third enum, EntryStatus { PENDING, DONE, SKIPPED }. A task can be SKIPPED as well as DONE, and EntryCompletion.status records it.
Identity columns: `uid` is a unique cross-device key and `id` is autoGenerate. A merge must key on uid, and parentEntryId, originalEntryId and sourceRowId travel as uids.

Deletion columns: Entry.deletedAt is a soft-delete with a Trash view, and updatedAt orders the merge. Reminder.deletedAt is a tombstone that wins on any device, with no updatedAt. EntryCompletion has no deletedAt and is append-only.

Three more columns pack a second meaning into entries: originalEntryId, originalOccurrenceDate and isExceptionSkip make an Entry row double as a single-occurrence exception or skip tombstone of a recurring base. Queries that list tasks must also exclude originalEntryId != null, as DayTimeline, ReviewPlanner and Tray do.
`startDate` and `startTime` are shared by both kinds. For a task they mean the planned When, not a span start, and Calendar draws tasks from them. `dueDate` is the separate deadline.

The kind/rule correspondence (Fixed for EVENT, Elastic for TASK) is not enforced. SnapshotMappers rebuilds the rule from a tag with no cross-check, so a TASK can carry Fixed and resolves as a one-off.

A recurring task is one live row. Resolving writes an EntryCompletion, then advances startDate by whole periods until it is in the future and resets status to PENDING. Missed occurrences are skipped, so an Elastic task does not go overdue per occurrence. The name Elastic is a documented misnomer kept for the persisted "ELASTIC:" tag.

Entry has more provenance and identity columns: source (EntrySource: MANUAL, DATABASE_SYNC, GOOGLE_CALENDAR, CALENDAR), sourceRowId (Database row link), googleEventId (retired, but still carried by the merge), providerEventId (per-device, excluded from the snapshot) and calendarKey (travels). GOOGLE_CALENDAR also keeps a row out of the Calendar Provider mirror.

Every Entry column by kind. Both kinds: id, uid, title, kind, startDate, startTime, recurrenceRule (Fixed for EVENT, Elastic for TASK), originalEntryId, originalOccurrenceDate, isExceptionSkip, sourceRowId, deletedAt, source, googleEventId, providerEventId, calendarKey, createdAt, updatedAt. EVENT only: endDate, endTime. TASK only: status, dueDate, parentEntryId, estimate, importance.
Subtasks are one level deep. TaskTree follows only a root's direct children, and a child's own parentEntryId is never followed.
